_comment: sourceRoot is resolved relative to the LabDeploy folder. Edit paths to match your environment.
_detection_notes: Each app checks known 'paths' first (fast). If 'searchExe' is set, it also searches Program Files recursively as a fallback (slower but catches non-standard installs). Optional 'pathMustMatch' is a regex the full path of a fallback-search hit must match -- use it when searchExe is a generic name (like java.exe) that other products also ship.
_progress_notes: Optional install.expectedSizeMB enables an estimated progress bar: percent is computed from disk space consumed during the install vs. this value (capped at 95%). After a real install, check the install.process_exited log event's diskDeltaMB field and update expectedSizeMB to that number for accurate bars.
_uninstall_notes: Optional 'uninstall' block overrides the default registry-based uninstall. method 'launch' opens 'program' (a vendor manager, e.g. NI Package Manager) and hands off to the user - used for software that hides itself from Windows Programs & Features. The optional 'message' is shown after launching.
_label_notes: Optional install.methodLabel overrides the card's install-type tag (default labels: Winget Install / File Copy / MSI Install / Silent EXE / Interactive Install). Use for special cases like big vendor images.
_installlast_notes: Batch order is a single stable rank sort: rank 0 = normal, 10 = install.installLast (heavy/licence-fiddly), 20 = methodLabel contains 'interactive' (needs a human). install.installOrder=N OVERRIDES all of them - lower runs earlier - and is how MATLAB(90)/MatlabArduino(100) are pinned to the last two slots. Ties keep on-screen (rooms.json) order. Every run logs the resolved order as installall.order.
_offload_notes: install.offload=true (exe/msi only) copies the app's top-level source folder to local disk, installs from there, then deletes it - faster/more reliable for big vendor images. The 'Offload big installers' checkbox toggles the feature; it also auto-falls-back to installing from the drive if local free space < (image size + expectedSizeMB + 3GB margin). Uses {source}/{file} arg placeholders, which resolve to the local copy.
_method_notes: install.method values: winget, copy, exe, msi, msix, psadt. 'msix' provisions an .msix machine-wide (Add-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online); pair it with detect.method 'appx' + a detect.packageName (the MSIX Identity Name) so detection/uninstall can find it. ZIP payloads are handled by pre-extracting into sources and using copy (portable apps) or exe (zip-with-inner-installer) - there is no runtime zip method.

The Add-On Explorer route REQUIRES an interactive login, which is exactly why it could never be scripted. MathWorks' own CLI installer (mpm.exe, 78.7 MB, Authenticode-signed by The MathWorks, shipped in MatlabImage\) needs no account. SEPARATE CARD ON PURPOSE (2026-07-28): the MATLAB card is untouched, a failure here is retryable in seconds instead of re-running a 46-minute 30 GB install, and detection reports Arduino support independently. requires:MATLAB installs MATLAB first if missing; installLast keeps it after MATLAB in a batch. TWO BUGS FOUND AND FIXED IN BENCH TESTING 2026-07-28 - both would have failed on the FIRST attempt on every machine: (1) --release is MANDATORY; without it mpm exits instantly with 'Error: Option --release is required but missing.' The batch now derives the release from the MATLAB folder name so a version bump cannot break it. (2) If --matlabroot does not point at a REAL MATLAB, mpm concludes MATLAB is missing and installs THE ENTIRE PRODUCT - a test against an empty folder pulled 5.8 GB / 153,450 files before being killed. The batch now refuses to call mpm unless <matlabroot> in\matlab.exe exists (exit 33). LabVIEW._quietTasks_note: Scheduled tasks to DISABLE so this app's updater stops nagging. Declaring this array puts a 'Quiet Updater' button on the card (installed apps only) and is the ONLY thing that turns the feature on - the other 41 cards are untouched. NI case (2026-07-29): ~30 min after install, NI Update Service pops a window advertising 2 critical updates it cannot install (21.0 predates NI's move to .nipkg, so it just points at ni.com/r/nilmrn). It is NOT optional to install: the feed index lists ni-update-service under Depends: for both ni-visa-sysapi and ni-labview-2021-cdsim-module-shared-x86, and 'nipkg remove ni-update-service' refuses with "Package 'ni-visa (21.0.0.49308)' requires 'ni-update-service'" - removing it would cost VISA, i.e. ELVIS III. Disabling its two tasks keeps the dependency satisfied and kills the only trigger. Task names have NO SPACES - verified on the bench; NI's own KB writes them as 'NI Update Service Check Task', which matches nothing. install-labview.bat does the same thing at the end of every install; this button is the retrofit for machines that already had LabVIEW.

ImageJ._NASPROD_SHORTCUT_TRAP:
DO NOT RE-COPY THIS PAYLOAD FROM POSTDEPLOY. Three separate runbooks (10104, 10105, 10106) shout the same warning in capitals: '>MAKE SURE IT'S POINTING TO THE C: DRIVE AND NOT NASPROD<'. Verified 2026-08-06 why they bother - postdeploy's own ImageJ folders contain TWO shortcuts with near-identical names:
    10103\ImageJ\ImageJ.lnk ............. -> \\fileserver\labtechs\Postdeploy\10103\ImageJ\ImageJ.exe   BAD
    10106\ImageJ\ImageJ.lnk ............. -> \\fileserver\labtechs\Postdeploy\10106\ImageJ\ImageJ.exe   BAD
    10105\ImageJ\ImageJ - Shortcut.lnk .. -> C:\Program Files\ImageJ\ImageJ.exe                        good
    10106\ImageJ\ImageJ - Shortcut.lnk .. -> C:\Program Files\ImageJ\ImageJ.exe                        good
A tech told to 'copy the shortcut in that folder' has a coin-flip chance of taking the network one, and a laptop that leaves the building then has an ImageJ icon that does nothing.
OUR STAGED PAYLOAD IS CLEAN: Science\ImageJ\ImageJ.lnk points at C:\Program Files\ImageJ\ImageJ.exe. LabDeploy is immune to this by construction anyway - the copy lands in C:\Program Files\ImageJ and the shortcut engine aims at the DETECTED local exe rather than at any shipped .lnk. Only a well-meaning manual re-copy from postdeploy could reintroduce it.

START EARLY, ON THE RUNBOOK'S INSTRUCTION. postdeploy 10104 software.txt step 3 says of JASP: 'start this early, it'll take a while', and 10106's says 'Start JASP first, it takes the longest'. At 2500 MB expected it is comfortably the largest science payload, so front-loading it lets the long pole run while smaller cards finish. installOrder 10 puts it ahead of everything else (MATLAB is 90, the config/shortcut cards are 95, MatlabArduino 100).

RavenLite._shortcut_bug_note: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-18, verified live on DEV-DESKTOP. detect.searchExe was "RavenLite.exe" (no space); the real installed exe is "Raven Lite.exe" (WITH a space). Neither detect path matched the real install folder either - it is "C:\Program Files\Raven Lite 2" (no version suffix), confirmed from the machine's own uninstall registry entry (InstallLocation) AND a directory listing. Traced end to end: (1) detection survived only on Test-AppInstalled's Phase-1.5 uninstall-registry fallback, so the card looked fine; (2) Resolve-AppExePath's primary lookup (Get-ChildItem -Filter searchExe) always missed, so it fell through to its 'biggest .exe in the folder' heuristic, which picks RavenHelper.exe (6.08 MB) over the real app Raven Lite.exe (0.86 MB); (3) New-AppShortcut therefore pointed the Public Desktop icon at RavenHelper.exe. Clicking that icon runs Raven's licensing/companion helper rather than the application - which is almost certainly the report that 'the RavenLite card opens Raven Pro'. Both fields below are corrected from live evidence. Rooms sharing this card: SCI1-209, SCI1-212, SCI1-310, SCI1-311, SCI1-316.
RavenLite._shortcut_bug_caveat: FRESH INSTALLS ONLY. Test-AppShortcut decides 'is this shortcut ours' by folder membership (does the .lnk target start with the install directory), not by exact filename - and RavenHelper.exe does live inside the correct folder. So a machine that already carries the RavenHelper-targeted icon still reports its shortcut as present and Repair will not replace it. Already-imaged Raven Lite machines need the desktop icon deleted once, then Refresh, to pick this up.
RavenLite._shortcutTarget_note: Raven Lite 2's folder contains TWO large exes: RavenHelper.exe (6.08 MB, the licensing/companion helper) and Raven Lite.exe (0.86 MB, the actual application). Resolve-AppExePath's last-resort heuristic is 'biggest .exe in the folder', which picks the helper - so naming the real exe here is what makes both the shortcut target and the strict check deterministic rather than size-dependent.
RavenLite._shortcutTargetStrict_note: Opts this card into the exact-exe shortcut check added to Test-AppShortcut 2026-08-18. Without it, folder membership alone counts as 'shortcut present', and the RavenHelper-targeted icon on already-imaged machines is blessed as correct - Verify Shortcuts said OK while the icon launched the wrong program. With it, Test-AppShortcut reports Present=False and Repair Shortcut / Verify Shortcuts replaces the icon with one aimed at Raven Lite.exe. Opt-in because eight other cards declare shortcutTarget and must keep their existing fuzzy behaviour.

WHAT THE REPLAY ACTUALLY PRODUCES IS UNVERIFIED - nobody has watched it. It may install a second Logger Pro alongside, or repair/downgrade the existing one. Python._path_field_report: 2026-08-21: "It throws the correct version but the execution app alias is defaulting to a local version that isn't added to path". DIAGNOSIS: not an alias problem. Windows ships 0-byte App Execution Alias stubs for python.exe/python3.exe in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps, and that folder is on every user's USER path. Windows searches SYSTEM path entries BEFORE user ones, so on a healthy machine the real interpreter shadows the stub - confirmed on the bench, where `where.exe python` lists C:\Program Files\Python313\python.exe (105816 bytes) ahead of the WindowsApps stub (0 bytes). The stub can only win when the real Python is ABSENT FROM THE SYSTEM PATH. So the bug is a missing system PATH entry.
Python._why_prependpath_can_miss: PrependPath=1 is passed on every run and is correct, but it is applied on a FRESH install only. When the installer finds the same version already present it runs in modify/repair mode and does not re-apply the PATH options - and the field logs show several Python runs that exited 0 in about 12 seconds having consumed no disk, which are repairs, not installs. A pre-existing PER-USER Python (student-installed, or baked into an image) produces the same end state: `python --version` answers correctly while nothing is on the system path. THIS card cannot detect any of that - detect:path only proves python.exe exists on disk, which is true either way. That is what the separate PythonPath card is for.
Python._recovery_for_existing_machines: The fix is a SEPARATE card, PythonPath, rather than a post-install hook on this one. Reasons: (1) it is visible - a tech sees its own red row saying the PATH is wrong, instead of a subtitle on a green card; (2) its detect method (envpath) re-reads the real system PATH on EVERY scan, so it is ground truth, where a post-install marker would only record that the step once ran and would keep claiming success after someone edited PATH; (3) install.requires=Python makes it unusable-before-Python by construction, and the engine installs Python first if it is missing. Windows searches SYSTEM path entries before USER ones, so a correct system PATH makes the stubs harmless - the smaller and more durable intervention. install._prereq_idea_unproven:
AN ESCAPE ROUTE EXISTS BUT IS NOT PROVEN AND CARRIES A NASTY FAILURE MODE. SpectroFlo installs SQL Server 2019 Express as the named instance RAINBOWDB (registry: MSSQL15.RAINBOWDB) with LoginMode=2, i.e. MIXED authentication - so it logs in with a SQL username/password, not Windows auth. If SQL were pre-installed by its own prerequisite card, SpectroFlo would probably detect it and skip both the extractor and the prompt.
WHY IT WAS NOT DONE: we know the instance name and the auth mode, but NOT the login and password SpectroFlo expects - they are not in SpectroFlo.exe.config (only boilerplate .NET client-services entries) and are presumably embedded in the app. Get that wrong and you get the worst outcome available: SpectroFlo installs silently, the card goes green, and it cannot reach its database - discovered by a student mid-class rather than by a tech at imaging time. A visible prompt is a better failure than a silent one.
install._ATTENDED_ON_PURPOSE:
RUNS INTERACTIVELY, WITH NO SWITCHES. This is a deliberate reversal, 2026-08-06, after two field observations - and silent mode turned out to be WORSE than no silent mode at all.

WHAT WE TRIED: /s /f1"setup.iss" /f2"..." /SMS, with a response file recorded via /r.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, in order:
  1. The card first prompts 'Choose Directory For Extracted Files' - that dialog belongs to the BUNDLED SQL Server Express SELF-EXTRACTOR (SQLEXPR_x64_ENU.exe), which SpectroFlo launches internally. A setup.iss can only answer SpectroFlo's own InstallShield dialogs, never a nested third-party extractor, so no response file can ever suppress it.
  2. WORSE: after answering it, SQL Server's OWN full setup UI opens - instance name, features, authentication mode, service accounts, the lot. Under an interactive run SpectroFlo drives SQL setup automatically and none of that is shown. The parameter-passing is evidently tied to dialog code that /s suppresses, so silent mode strips SpectroFlo of the ability to configure its own database and dumps a raw SQL wizard on the tech.

WHY THAT IS DANGEROUS, not merely annoying: SpectroFlo needs the instance named RAINBOWDB with LoginMode=2 (mixed auth) and a SQL login whose credentials are embedded in the app and unknown to us. A tech completing that wizard by hand will almost certainly produce an installation SpectroFlo cannot connect to - and it will look successful until someone opens the app.

So: no switches. The installer behaves exactly as it did when the response file was recorded - SQL Express installs itself correctly and unattended, and the tech answers only SpectroFlo's own questions. setup.iss is kept in the payload folder as evidence of what was tried; it is NOT used.

install._why_scripted_not_copy:
CHANGED FROM method:copy TO A SCRIPT, 2026-08-06, after a field test proved copy was not enough.

WHAT HAPPENED on 10108LAB31-01: the wizard was deliberately answered the Instrument Configurations wizard WRONGLY, then let this card run. The card copied the right files and went green - correctly, they genuinely were byte-identical - but SpectroFlo still failed to launch with 'Fail to start instrument service'.

CORRECTION, 2026-08-06 (later the same day): the duplicate-xml theory below explains the DUPLICATE, but it was almost certainly NOT the cause of that error message. The real cause was this card deploying a 3.3.0 SpectroFlo.exe.config onto a 3.0.3 install, which stripped UseLocalInstrumentServices=true - see _exe_config_excluded. The replace-not-overlay behaviour described below is still correct and worth keeping; just do not credit it with having fixed the instrument-service error, because it did not.

THE CAUSE: LabDeploy's copy method is ADDITIVE and never deletes at the destination (a deliberate safety rule - a wrong destination running unattended could wipe the wrong folder). SpectroFlo had written its OWN instrument xml from the wrong answers, and the copy ADDED ours beside it. Two instrument configs in Configuration\, and the instrument service cannot resolve which machine it is meant to be.

Apply-InstrumentConfig.ps1 therefore REPLACES rather than overlays. Its safety rules, all tested:
  * refuses unless SpectroFlo.exe is actually present (exit 1)
  * refuses unless EXACTLY ONE instrument xml is staged - ambiguity means do nothing (exit 2)
  * strays are MOVED to Configuration-replaced-<timestamp>\, never hard-deleted
  * scope is Configuration\*.xml only, non-recursive, nothing else touched
  * verifies the end state by hash and that exactly one xml remains, failing loudly otherwise (exit 3)
  * idempotent - re-running on a correct machine changes nothing
The keeper filename is READ FROM THE STAGED FOLDER, not hardcoded, so switching instrument means replacing the staged xml and nothing else.
install._self_healing: autoFollow means ANY SpectroFlo install or reinstall re-runs this automatically, so a stray config introduced by a later manual reinstall gets cleaned without anyone remembering to do it.
install._user_config_excluded:
user.config was REMOVED from the managed set 2026-08-06, after watching SpectroFlo overwrite it.
Observed on the bench: the card copied user.config with OrganizedByDate=True at 11:21; SpectroFlo was opened and closed at 13:11; by 13:12 the app had rewritten the file back to false and added elements our copy never had (568 -> 653 bytes). SpectroFlo OWNS that file and rewrites it from its own in-memory settings on exit.
Leaving it managed would have been actively harmful: detection is a byte-for-byte match, so the card would flip RED the first time anyone opened SpectroFlo and stay red on every laptop forever - reporting normal app behaviour as drift, and training people to ignore red cards.
STILL MANAGED: the instrument xml only, under Configuration-Laser-B14.xml and SpectroFlo.exe.config.

install._exe_config_excluded:
SpectroFlo.exe.config was REMOVED from the managed set 2026-08-06, after it was PROVEN to be the cause of "Fail to start instrument service". THIS CARD WAS BREAKING SPECTROFLO.

PROOF, from SpectroFlo ApplicationLog on DEV-DESKTOP. 3.0.3 installed and launched fine TWICE, then this card ran, and every launch after it failed:
  15:37:37  Application Startup. Version: 3.0.3(11292021)   fine
  15:37:48  Application Startup. Version: 3.0.3(11292021)   fine
  15:38:11  this card runs - "copied 2 config file(s) into place"
  15:38:57  Application Startup. Version: 3.3.0(12282023)   BROKEN

WHY. The staged copy was captured from the bench earlier that same day, while SpectroFlo 3.3.0 was installed on it. SpectroFlo.exe.config is VERSION-SPECIFIC VENDOR PLUMBING, not a settings file. Diffed against the pristine file extracted from the cached MSI, 3.3.0s config is SMALLER (12163 vs 14557 bytes) because it DROPS seven keys 3.0.3 requires:
    UseLocalInstrumentServices       true  -> ABSENT
    ShowInstrumentServiceCMDWindow   true  -> ABSENT
    DatabaseMigrationEnabled         true  -> ABSENT
    AnalysisApi                      Rainbow.Analysis.AnalysisController -> ABSENT
    SkipLoginPassword                true  -> ABSENT
    DAQDelayTime / IsDebugMode             -> ABSENT
  plus SoftwareVersion 3.0.3->3.3.0 and SoftwareBuild 11292021->12282023.
UseLocalInstrumentServices=true is literally what tells SpectroFlo to start a LOCAL instrument service. Strip it and the app cannot start one - that is the error text, verbatim.
DatabaseMigrationEnabled=true is a strong suspect for the separate "no database" failure on 10108LAB31-01 the same day, which was chased for hours as a SQL Server / domain password-policy problem and may never have been one.

THE PUNCHLINE: the ONLY reason this file was ever managed was to force EnableWorklist=false (runbook question 5). Pristine 3.0.3 ALREADY ships EnableWorklist=false. Deploying it bought nothing and cost a working install.

RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: never deploy a vendors application config across versions. Only deploy files that hold OUR settings and nothing else. Configuration\\1-Laser-B14.xml qualifies; SpectroFlo.exe.config does not.

RECOVERY for a machine this already damaged: copy Science\\SpectroFlo\\_not-managed\\SpectroFlo.exe.config.PRISTINE-3.0.3 over C:\\Program Files\\Cytekbio\\SpectroFlo\\SpectroFlo.exe.config. That file is 3.0.3 ONLY. To spot a damaged machine, read the Application Startup version in C:\\CytekbioExport\\ApplicationLog_<MM YYYY>.txt - registry saying 3.0.3 while the log says 3.3.0 means this bug hit it.

install._silent_suspect:
SAME BUG CLASS AS QUANTSTUDIO, found 2026-08-06. This binary carries ISSetup.dll, i.e. it is an InstallShield INSTALLSCRIPT project. For that project type '/s' means 'replay the recorded response file setup.iss', NOT 'be quiet', and '/v' (pass-through to msiexec) is Basic-MSI syntax this project never uses. So the current arguments do not make it silent. Proven for SpectroFlo on this bench: the card launched with /s /v"/qn REBOOT=ReallySuppress" and the installer put an interactive 'Choose Directory For Extracted Files' dialog on screen for its bundled SQL Server Express.
THE FIX, same recipe that worked for QuantStudio:
  1. setup.exe /r /f1"C:\Temp\<app>.iss"   <- walk the wizard once
  2. ship the .iss beside the installer
  3. arguments: /s /f1"{source}\Science\<folder>\setup.iss" /f2"%TEMP%\<app>-silent.log" /SMS
  4. confirm ResultCode=0 in the /f2 log
/SMS matters: InstallShield setup.exe otherwise returns in seconds while the install continues in the background, and LabDeploy declares success early - QuantStudio went green 28 seconds before its install finished, and the app errored when opened in that window.
KINESIS IS UNTESTED but carries the same ISSetup.dll marker, so treat its current '/s /v"/qn REBOOT=ReallySuppress"' as probably-not-silent until a real 249A run proves otherwise. Its payload is fully compressed and cannot be inspected without running it, so the field test is the only way to know.

Do not 'fix' the missing quotes. LabDeploy launches exe cards through cmd /c with the whole command already quoted, so this survives the trip.

The alternatives are a UNIV classroom/educational licence (JetBrains grants these free to universities; it produces an activation code or a licence-server URL that CAN be pre-seeded) or a paid seat. The real application still unpacks into each user's profile the first time THAT user launches it - a few seconds of 'installing' on first run, then normal. That is the vendor's design and there is no machine-wide runtime available. It is fine on a lab laptop; it just means the first launch of a fresh student profile is slow and needs a moment of network. It also means detection can only ever prove the stub is present - which is the honest limit of what the image can guarantee.

install._note: Office Deployment Tool. setup.exe /configure with the XML next to it; Visio\Visio-Config.xml carries the full explanation of every setting. install._unresolved_sku: ONE FIELD IN THE XML IS UNVERIFIED: the Product ID. It is set to VisioProRetail (Visio Plan 2, per-user Microsoft 365 assignment) because that is what the guide's own support link describes - but if UNIV licenses Visio through a CSU volume agreement it must be VisioProXVolume or VisioStdXVolume instead, and the wrong one either refuses to install or installs a Visio nobody can activate. Ask whoever owns the Microsoft 365 tenant before the first machine.
install._shared_computer_activation: Visio-Config.xml sets SharedComputerLicensing=1, and on a cart laptop that is not optional. Without it the FIRST student to open Visio burns one of their five personal device activations on a machine they will never see again, and every student after them is locked out. This is the difference between Visio working all semester and Visio working for one afternoon.
install._channel_must_match: Click-to-Run allows exactly ONE channel and ONE bitness per machine. The XML says Current / 64-bit, which matches a standard Microsoft 365 Apps image. If the 5105 image ships a different channel, setup.exe refuses and the card fails with a channel-mismatch error rather than anything obviously Visio-shaped - check HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Office\ClickToRun\Configuration on machine 1 before blaming the card.
install._offline_option: With no local payload, setup.exe streams 1-4 GB from Microsoft's CDN per machine. For a full cart, run `setup.exe /download Visio-Config.xml` once on the bench FROM INSIDE the Visio folder - it creates an Office\ subfolder next to setup.exe, and in /configure mode with SourcePath omitted the ODT uses that local folder first, falling back to the CDN only if it is absent. NO XML edit and no absolute path needed (stick drive letters vary, and nothing expands {source}-style placeholders inside the XML - only install.arguments gets that treatment). Same reasoning that moved PuTTY off winget. Confirm on machine 1: an offline install starts copying immediately instead of showing download progress.
